title: Pointers to Pointers and argv
summary: A pointer is a variable too, so it has an address, and a pointer to a pointer (char **) lets a function move the caller's pointer. An array of strings is an array of char pointers, and main's argc and argv are exactly that - the words typed after the program's name. Sorting strings means swapping pointers, not text.

cards.q: int **pp = &p; where p points at x. What is **pp?
cards.a:
x

Follow pp to p, then p to x.

cards.q: Why does a function take char **cursor instead of char *cursor?
cards.a:
So it can move the caller's pointer

The same reason swap takes int *.

cards.q: With ./tool one two, what is argc?
const char *names[] = {"a", "bb"}; - what does the array hold?
cards.a:
Two pointers to text stored elsewhere

An array of strings is an array of pointers.
